releaseNotes: Platform release: a company can now argue about its own record inside Formation. Conversations attach to a claim, a decision, a deliverable, one section of a deliverable, or a workstream; a reviewer can start one, because an advisor brought in to question the record has to be able to say so and that is the whole reason the reviewer role exists. Replies join their conversation rather than nesting deeper, resolving a thread settles it without deleting it, and nobody edits or deletes words they did not write at any role — an owner who can rewrite what an advisor said is an owner who can rewrite the history of a decision.

The rule the whole feature is built to hold is that a comment is never a source of truth. The moment a company's actual answer lives in a thread, the record stops being the record and everything downstream of it is reading the wrong document. So comments are load-bearing for people and inert for the system: they do not move readiness, they are not weighed as evidence, they never reach a provider request, and they never reach a shared link. Two tests assert the last two directly — not because either currently reads a comment, but because both are built by naming fields, and the day somebody adds a convenient spread is the day a private argument between cofounders lands in an investor's browser. Mentions resolve to members of the same company and nowhere else, and the surface says plainly that a mention is found here rather than sent, because Formation still has no mail transport. Schema 6 adds the collection. Checks, 199 domain tests, the production build, and the full audit pass.
